name: Wars
description: The wars that shaped the world, from the first empires to the two world wars, the Cold War, and the wars and trade wars of today.

checkpoints.name: Ancient wars
checkpoints.note: The first kings fight over rivers and trade. Greece holds off Persia, Alexander marches to India, Rome defeats Carthage and Qin unites China by force. Rome holds its frontiers for centuries and then loses the West.

checkpoints.name: Medieval wars
checkpoints.note: Arab armies carry Islam from Spain to Central Asia, Vikings raid the coasts of Europe and crusaders fight for Jerusalem. The Mongols conquer the largest land empire ever, and England and France fight for a hundred years.

checkpoints.name: Gunpowder empires
checkpoints.note: Ottoman cannon take Constantinople and Spain conquers the Aztecs and Incas. Wars of religion tear Europe apart until the Peace of Westphalia, and Britain and France fight across the world for empire.

checkpoints.name: Revolutions and empires
checkpoints.note: Revolutions in America and France bring citizen armies, and Napoleon conquers most of Europe. Britain fights China over opium, the United States fights its Civil War, and Germany and Japan rise through war.

checkpoints.name: World War I
checkpoints.note: An assassination in Sarajevo pulls the great powers into war. Millions die in the trenches of the Western Front, revolution takes Russia out of the war, and the entry of the United States helps end it in November 1918.

checkpoints.name: Between the wars
checkpoints.note: The peace treaties leave bitter grievances. The Soviet Union is born from revolution and civil war, Hitler builds Nazi Germany, Japan invades China, Spain falls into civil war and at Munich Europe tries to buy peace.

checkpoints.name: World War II
checkpoints.note: The deadliest war in history, from the invasion of Poland to Hiroshima. Germany overruns Europe and attacks the Soviet Union, Japan strikes Pearl Harbor, six million Jews are murdered in the Holocaust, and the Allies win in 1945.

checkpoints.name: The Cold War
checkpoints.note: The United States and the Soviet Union face each other with nuclear weapons but never fight directly. Their rivalry fuels wars in Korea, Vietnam and Afghanistan and crises in Berlin and Cuba, and ends when the Soviet Union breaks up.

checkpoints.name: After the Cold War
checkpoints.note: Yugoslavia breaks apart in war, genocide strikes Rwanda and war engulfs Congo. The attacks of 11 September 2001 lead the United States into long wars in Afghanistan and Iraq.

checkpoints.name: Wars of today
checkpoints.note: The Arab Spring turns into civil war in Syria and Libya and the rise of ISIS. Russia seizes Crimea and invades Ukraine, war returns to Gaza, Israel and Iran exchange strikes, Sudan collapses, and tariffs start new trade wars.
